nodes.label: Cross-stock fifteen-minute qualifying-entry study
nodes.rationale: Runs FTFT, SES and TE in separate $1,000 alternative cash accounts across nine dates while preserving qualifying entries. FTFT supplies one losing trade; SES and TE supply no trades, so the study does not establish traded cross-stock performance.

nodes.label: Fifteen-minute exit-request deadline
nodes.rationale: The primary timer disables original price exits and requests liquidation 900 seconds after the actual fill. Nominal completion took 901.349644012 seconds and lost $63.726, with routing and future capacity governing completion. Original reward/risk remains only an admission filter, and unresolved close-of-session exposure would stop the branch rather than create a sale.

nodes.label: SES and TE admission rejections
nodes.rationale: SES's 26 alerts and TE's 28 alerts yielded no orders because of reward/risk, empty price intervals, stale quotes and session-time restrictions. Separate accounts eliminate cash competition but cannot eliminate admission failures. Their zero account P&L is distinct from an unavailable trade-return estimate.
